intent.raw_query: Bali for solo traveler, $1500 budget, beaches and yoga, July 2026 from LA

experiences.name: Sunrise Yoga at Campuhan Ridge Walk
experiences.description: Join an outdoor sunrise yoga session along the scenic Campuhan Ridge Walk in Ubud, surrounded by lush jungle and rice paddies. Many local instructors offer small group classes here, combining gentle flow yoga with breathtaking natural views. A deeply restorative and spiritual experience unique to Bali.

experiences.name: Seminyak Beach Sunset & Surf Lesson
experiences.description: Take a beginner-friendly surf lesson on the golden sands of Seminyak Beach, one of Bali's most beautiful and accessible surf spots. After your lesson, relax and watch the legendary Bali sunset with a fresh coconut in hand. Local surf schools provide boards and instructors at very affordable rates.

experiences.name: Balinese Cooking Class & Market Tour
experiences.description: Start your morning at a traditional local market in Ubud, guided by a Balinese chef who helps you select fresh spices, vegetables, and proteins. Then head to an open-air kitchen to learn how to prepare classic dishes like nasi goreng, satay lilit, and black rice pudding. A delicious cultural immersion.

experiences.name: Multi-Day Yoga Retreat at The Yoga Barn
experiences.description: Spend several days immersed in Bali's world-famous wellness hub, The Yoga Barn in Ubud. Choose from daily drop-in classes including Hatha, Vinyasa, Yin, and meditation. The lush jungle setting, community atmosphere, and variety of teachers make this a transformative experience perfectly suited for a 13-day stay.

experiences.name: Nusa Penida Island Day Trip & Kelingking Beach
experiences.description: Take a fast boat from Sanur to the stunning island of Nusa Penida and visit the iconic Kelingking Beach, known for its dramatic T-Rex shaped cliff and turquoise waters. Snorkel at Crystal Bay, spot manta rays, and explore pristine beaches largely untouched by mass tourism. One of Bali's most breathtaking natural escapes.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Bali
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Ngurah Rai International Airport at 22:30. Take a pre-booked airport shuttle or grab a Grab/Gojek ride to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get settled into your beachfront accommodation.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In transit
meals.lunch: N/A - In transit
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night snack from a 24-hour warung (local food stall) near the resort or order from a budget-friendly local delivery app. Try nasi goreng (fried rice) for around IDR 25,000–40,000.

day_by_day.notes: Keep your first night simple. Pre-download Grab or Gojek apps before landing for cheap airport transfers. Exchange a small amount of currency at the airport for immediate needs, but use ATMs in town for better rates. Rest is the priority tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely wake-up, take your first walk along the beachfront directly from the resort. Explore the shoreline, breathe in the ocean air, and get oriented with your surroundings. Watch local fishermen and enjoy the warm 25°C morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the nearest local market or beach town on foot or by rented bicycle (IDR 50,000–80,000/day). Visit a local warung for lunch, then spend the afternoon relaxing on the beach. Swim in the calm warm waters and soak up the Bali sunshine.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the famous Bali sunset from the beach. Head to a nearby beachside warung for dinner and enjoy the laid-back evening atmosphere. Stroll along the beach strip and plan the days ahead.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the resort if breakfast is included, or find a nearby warung serving nasi goreng or bubur ayam (chicken porridge) for IDR 20,000–35,000.
meals.lunch: Local warung lunch — try mie goreng (fried noodles) or gado-gado (peanut sauce salad) for IDR 25,000–45,000.
meals.dinner: Beachside warung dinner — grilled fish or satay with rice and vegetables for IDR 40,000–70,000. Look for 'nasi campur' (mixed rice) for great value.

day_by_day.notes: Stay hydrated in the warm weather. Buy a large refillable water bottle from a local minimart (Indomaret or Alfamart) to save money. Rent a bicycle for easy and cheap local exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Join a sunrise beach yoga session. Many budget-friendly yoga studios and beach instructors in Bali offer morning classes starting at IDR 80,000–150,000. Check with the resort reception for nearby recommendations or search for free community yoga sessions on the beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby Hindu temple close to the beachfront area. Dress respectfully (sarong required — often available to borrow or rent for IDR 10,000–20,000). Explore the temple grounds and learn about Balinese culture and spirituality.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Kecak fire dance performance at a nearby cultural venue (tickets IDR 100,000–150,000). This is an unmissable Bali cultural experience. Afterward, grab dinner at a local warung.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit smoothie bowl at a budget café — IDR 35,000–55,000. Bali is famous for its affordable healthy breakfast options.
meals.lunch: Pack a simple picnic from the local minimart or grab babi guling (suckling pig) or nasi jinggo (small rice parcels) from a street vendor for IDR 15,000–30,000.
meals.dinner: Warung dinner near the cultural venue — nasi campur or ayam betutu (slow-cooked chicken) for IDR 35,000–60,000.

day_by_day.notes: Bring a light sarong for temple visits — it's a must. Morning yoga on the beach is often cooler and more comfortable before 8:00 AM. Check for free or donation-based yoga events on community boards.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a scooter (IDR 70,000–100,000/day with fuel) and head to a quieter, less touristy beach nearby. Explore hidden coves and enjoy snorkeling in the crystal-clear warm water. Bring your own snorkel gear if possible, or rent locally for IDR 30,000–50,000.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue beach hopping along the coast. Find a shady spot, read a book, or simply relax and swim. The 25°C weather and minimal rainfall make this ideal for outdoor beach time.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area and join a sunset meditation or yoga session on the beach if available. Enjoy the golden hour light over the Indian Ocean.

meals.breakfast: Eat early before your scooter trip — try roti bakar (toasted bread with toppings) and kopi Bali (Balinese coffee) at a local café for IDR 20,000–35,000.
meals.lunch: Find a beachside warung at your snorkeling spot — fresh coconut water (IDR 15,000) and grilled corn or nasi goreng for IDR 25,000–45,000.
meals.dinner: Return to your favorite warung near the resort for a budget dinner. Try lawar (Balinese mixed salad with coconut) or soto ayam (chicken soup) for IDR 30,000–55,000.

day_by_day.notes: Always wear sunscreen and a rash guard when snorkeling. Check your scooter for damage before renting and take photos. Bring cash as many beach warungs don't accept cards. Stay aware of rip currents at unfamiliar beaches.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning yoga class at a well-known budget yoga studio. Bali has countless affordable studios offering drop-in classes for IDR 80,000–200,000. Focus on a restorative or hatha yoga session to recharge mid-trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a local arts and crafts market. Browse handmade jewelry, batik fabrics, wooden carvings, and souvenirs. Practice your bargaining skills — prices are always negotiable. Budget IDR 100,000–300,000 for small souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Take a traditional Balinese cooking class if budget allows (IDR 200,000–350,000 for a group class). You'll learn to make dishes like satay, tempeh, and sambal. Alternatively, enjoy a relaxed dinner at a local restaurant with live traditional music.

meals.breakfast: Acai bowl or banana pancakes at a budget-friendly café popular with backpackers — IDR 35,000–60,000.
meals.lunch: Street food lunch at the market — try martabak (stuffed pancake), pisang goreng (fried banana), or bakso (meatball soup) for IDR 15,000–30,000.
meals.dinner: Cooking class dinner (included if you join a class) or warung dinner for IDR 40,000–65,000.

day_by_day.notes: Bargaining at markets is expected and part of the culture — start at 40–50% of the asking price. Group cooking classes are the most budget-friendly option and a great way to meet fellow travelers.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for a sunrise beach walk or light jog along the shore. The early morning is the coolest part of the day and perfect for exercise. Collect shells or simply enjoy the peaceful atmosphere before the beach gets busy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a budget day trip to explore nearby rice terraces or a waterfall accessible by scooter. Bali's lush green landscape is stunning in July. Entry fees for most natural attractions are IDR 10,000–30,000.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the beach for a relaxed evening. Find a beanbag café or low-key beach bar with cheap local Bintang beer (IDR 30,000–50,000) or fresh juice (IDR 20,000–35,000) and enjoy the stars.

meals.breakfast: Nasi goreng or bubur ayam at a local warung — IDR 20,000–35,000.
meals.lunch: Pack snacks from the minimart for your day trip — instant noodles, crackers, and fruit — total IDR 30,000–50,000.
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on a nicer warung dinner — try bebek betutu (slow-cooked duck) or fresh seafood for IDR 60,000–100,000.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable shoes for waterfall or rice terrace visits as paths can be slippery. Bring a light rain jacket just in case of brief afternoon showers — July sees about 30mm of rain for the month. Always bring cash to natural attractions.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recharge day. Sleep in, practice personal yoga on the beach or in your room, journal about your trip so far, and enjoy a slow breakfast. This is your halfway point — take it easy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local neighborhood on foot. Visit a local temple, a neighborhood banjar (community hall), or simply wander through residential streets to experience authentic Balinese daily life away from tourist areas.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a budget Balinese massage — traditional full-body massages are available for IDR 80,000–150,000/hour at local spas and street-front massage parlors. A perfect mid-trip treat.

meals.breakfast: Lazy breakfast at a café — try Balinese black rice pudding (bubur injin) with coconut milk for IDR 25,000–40,000.
meals.lunch: Warung lunch — try tempeh manis (sweet tempeh) and sayur urab (vegetable salad with coconut) for a vegetarian budget meal at IDR 25,000–45,000.
meals.dinner: Night market or local food court (pasar malam) dinner — explore multiple stalls and try a variety of dishes for IDR 40,000–70,000 total.

day_by_day.notes: Mid-trip rest days are important to avoid burnout. A traditional Balinese massage is one of the best budget splurges in Bali. Always check reviews before choosing a massage parlor for safety and quality.

day_by_day.morning: Join a group surf lesson on the beach. Bali is one of the world's best surfing destinations and beginner lessons are very affordable (IDR 150,000–250,000 including board rental for 2 hours). The warm water and gentle waves make it perfect for first-timers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue practicing surfing or switch to stand-up paddleboarding (SUP) rental for IDR 80,000–120,000/hour. Alternatively, relax on the beach and watch more experienced surfers.
day_by_day.evening: Join a beach bonfire gathering if available, or find a rooftop bar with budget cocktails and ocean views. Enjoy the warm evening breeze.

meals.breakfast: Eat a light but energizing breakfast before surfing — banana and peanut butter toast or a smoothie for IDR 25,000–40,000.
meals.lunch: Post-surf refuel at a beach warung — large portion of nasi campur with extra protein for IDR 35,000–55,000.
meals.dinner: Budget seafood dinner at a beachside warung — grilled fish, prawns, or squid with rice and vegetables for IDR 50,000–80,000.

day_by_day.notes: Apply waterproof sunscreen before surfing and reapply after each session. Book surf lessons through your resort or a reputable local surf school. Beginners should always surf with an instructor. Rash guards are recommended to prevent board rash and sunburn.

day_by_day.morning: Morning yoga session focusing on flexibility and mindfulness. If you've found a studio you love, return for another class. Alternatively, follow a free YouTube yoga session on the beach using your phone and portable speaker.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local organic farm or permaculture garden if available in the area. Many offer free or low-cost tours and sell fresh local produce. Stock up on tropical fruits like mangosteen, rambutan, and salak (snake fruit).
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost cultural event — Bali frequently hosts free temple ceremonies, traditional dance rehearsals, and community festivals that welcome respectful visitors. Ask your resort staff for local event recommendations.

meals.breakfast: Fresh tropical fruit platter with yogurt from a local café — IDR 30,000–50,000.
meals.lunch: Farm-fresh vegetarian meal if visiting an organic farm, or a healthy warung lunch with fresh vegetables for IDR 25,000–45,000.
meals.dinner: Local Balinese restaurant dinner — try a set menu (nasi campur bali) for a complete cultural food experience at IDR 40,000–70,000.

day_by_day.notes: Free temple ceremonies are a beautiful cultural experience but always be respectful — dress modestly, follow local customs, and never enter restricted areas. Ask permission before photographing ceremonies.

day_by_day.morning: Take a scooter or join a shared tour to explore a nearby coastal area or headland with panoramic ocean views. Bali's coastline is dramatic and beautiful, with cliffs, hidden beaches, and temples perched above the sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a beachside Hindu sea temple (pura segara). These coastal temples are architecturally stunning and spiritually significant. Spend time exploring the grounds and watching the waves crash against the rocks below.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cliff walk or viewpoint visit for golden hour photography. Then head back for a relaxed dinner and pack light for the next day's adventures.

meals.breakfast: Nasi goreng with a fried egg and kopi tubruk (traditional Balinese coffee) at a local warung — IDR 20,000–35,000.
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch with snacks from the minimart at the clifftop viewpoint — IDR 30,000–50,000.
meals.dinner: Warung dinner near the resort — try jukut ares (banana stem curry) or pepes ikan (fish in banana leaf) for an authentic local meal at IDR 35,000–60,000.

day_by_day.notes: Be cautious near cliff edges — some viewpoints lack safety railings. The 25°C weather is ideal for outdoor exploration. Bring plenty of water and snacks for full-day scooter trips. Check fuel levels before heading out.

day_by_day.morning: Final serious yoga day — attend a longer 90-minute yoga workshop or specialty class (IDR 120,000–200,000). Focus on a style you haven't tried yet, such as yin yoga, vinyasa flow, or pranayama breathwork.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at the beach for your last full beach day. Swim, snorkel, read, or simply lie in the warm Bali sun. Reflect on your journey and enjoy the moment.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge on a slightly nicer dinner to celebrate your last big evening. Find a restaurant with ocean views and try a Balinese set dinner for IDR 80,000–150,000. Toast to a wonderful trip.

meals.breakfast: Energizing pre-yoga breakfast — overnight oats or chia pudding at a health café for IDR 35,000–55,000.
meals.lunch: Beach warung lunch — fresh coconut water and a light meal for IDR 30,000–50,000.
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at a mid-range local restaurant with ocean views — grilled seafood platter or Balinese rijsttafel (rice table) for IDR 80,000–150,000.

day_by_day.notes: This is your last full beach and yoga day — make the most of it. Book your celebratory dinner in advance if possible as popular spots fill up quickly during peak season. July is Bali's high season so early reservations are wise.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise beach meditation or yoga on the sand. Take photos, collect last memories of the ocean, and enjoy a slow, mindful morning. Visit any spots you may have missed during the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at the local market. Stock up on Balinese spice mixes, coffee, sarongs, and handmade crafts to bring home. Budget IDR 100,000–300,000 for final gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner with any new friends made during the trip. Find a warung with communal seating and share a final Balinese meal together. Pack your bags and prepare for departure.

meals.breakfast: Slow breakfast at your favorite café discovered during the trip — IDR 30,000–55,000.
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the market — street food snacks and fresh juice for IDR 25,000–40,000.
meals.dinner: Farewell warung dinner — order all your favorite dishes from the trip for a final taste of Bali at IDR 40,000–70,000.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your checkout time with the resort. Many budget accommodations offer luggage storage if your flight is late. Keep some IDR cash for last-minute expenses and airport needs. Avoid eating anything unusual the night before your flight.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Arrange transport to Ngurah Rai International Airport via Grab/Gojek or a pre-arranged shuttle. Arrive at the airport at least 2–3 hours before your flight for international departures.
day_by_day.afternoon: Airport time — browse duty-free shops for last-minute Balinese coffee, chocolate, or Arak (local spirit) if budget allows. Relax at the airport and reflect on 13 incredible days in Bali.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Bali. Carry beautiful memories of beaches, yoga, culture, and the warm Balinese spirit with you.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the resort before checkout or grab something quick at a nearby warung — IDR 20,000–35,000.
meals.lunch: Airport food court lunch — Indonesian options available at IDR 50,000–100,000 (airport prices are higher than town).
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport restaurant depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Budget for airport departure tax if not included in your ticket. Keep your boarding pass and passport easily accessible. Grab/Gojek rides to the airport are significantly cheaper than metered taxis — book in advance. Arrive early as Bali airport can be busy during peak July season.

trip_options.title: Classic Bali Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Ngurah Rai International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and take a pre-arranged airport transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your beachfront room.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable
meals.lunch: Not applicable
meals.dinner: Light snack or room service at the resort upon arrival if hungry

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book your airport transfer in advance to avoid late-night taxi hassles. Keep a light snack in your carry-on for the journey. Rest well — your Bali adventure begins tomorrow!

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a slow morning at the resort. Take your first walk along the beachfront and watch the sunrise over the Indian Ocean. Get familiar with the resort facilities including the pool and yoga pavilion.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon relaxing on the resort's beachfront. Take a gentle swim in the calm warm waters (avg 25°C). Explore the immediate beach area, rent a sun lounger, and ease into the Bali rhythm. Visit a nearby beach shack for a fresh coconut.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the beach promenade at sunset. Enjoy a relaxed welcome dinner at the resort's beachside restaurant, soaking in your first Bali sunset.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet — fresh tropical fruits, eggs, and Balinese rice porridge (bubur)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a nearby warung (local eatery) — nasi campur (mixed rice) for around IDR 35,000–50,000
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's beachside restaurant — grilled fish with sambal and steamed rice, budget IDR 120,000–180,000

day_by_day.notes: Keep day 2 light and relaxed to recover from jet lag. Stay hydrated and apply sunscreen generously. The warm summer weather is ideal for beach time.

day_by_day.morning: Join an early morning sunrise yoga session on the resort's beachfront yoga pavilion (usually 7:00–8:30 AM). Many Bali resorts offer complimentary or low-cost yoga classes. Breathe in the ocean air and set your intentions for the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to a nearby surf school for a beginner or intermediate surfing lesson (approx. IDR 350,000–500,000 for a 2-hour group lesson including board and instructor). Bali's warm waters and consistent waves make it perfect for learning.
day_by_day.evening: Explore a nearby beach town (such as Seminyak or Kuta depending on resort location) for sunset cocktails at a beach club. Watch the famous Bali sunset with a Bintang beer or fresh mocktail.

meals.breakfast: Smoothie bowl and coffee at a local café near the resort — IDR 55,000–80,000
meals.lunch: Post-surf meal at a warung near the surf school — mie goreng (fried noodles) or gado-gado, IDR 30,000–50,000
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range beach club restaurant — grilled prawns, fresh salads, IDR 150,000–220,000

day_by_day.notes: Book your yoga session the evening before to secure a spot. Wear reef-safe sunscreen for surfing. Carry cash as many small surf schools and warungs don't accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: Take a guided snorkeling trip from the beach (departs around 8:00 AM). Explore vibrant coral reefs and tropical fish in Bali's clear warm waters. Many operators offer half-day trips from the beach for IDR 250,000–400,000 per person including equipment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a traditional Balinese market in the nearby town — browse handcrafted souvenirs, sarongs, incense, and spices. Practice gentle bargaining (a Bali cultural norm). Pick up some local snacks like klepon (green rice balls) or pisang goreng (fried banana).
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Kecak Fire Dance performance at a nearby temple or cultural venue (IDR 100,000–150,000). This iconic Balinese ritual dance performed at sunset is a must-see cultural experience.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the resort before the snorkeling trip — fruit, toast, and juice
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a beachside warung post-snorkeling — grilled fish with plecing kangkung (water spinach), IDR 60,000–90,000
meals.dinner: Pre-show dinner at a local mid-range restaurant near the cultural venue — bebek betutu (slow-cooked duck), IDR 120,000–180,000

day_by_day.notes: Book the snorkeling trip through your resort or a reputable local operator. Bring an underwater camera or rent a GoPro. The Kecak dance is performed outdoors so bring a light layer for the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Ubud — Bali's cultural heart (approx. 1–1.5 hours from coastal areas). Start with a visit to the Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary (IDR 80,000 entry). Walk through ancient temple grounds surrounded by over 700 long-tailed macaques.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ubud's famous Tegallalang Rice Terraces — walk along the stunning UNESCO-recognized stepped paddies. Enjoy the lush green landscape and take photos from the famous swing (IDR 50,000–100,000). Browse Ubud Art Market for local crafts and batik fabrics.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by early evening. Wind down with a traditional Balinese massage at a local spa near the resort (60 min full body massage, IDR 120,000–200,000). Enjoy a quiet dinner back at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before departing for Ubud
meals.lunch: Lunch at a mid-range organic café in Ubud — Balinese curry bowl or tempeh salad, IDR 80,000–130,000
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort or a nearby beachside restaurant — satay platter with peanut sauce and rice, IDR 100,000–160,000

day_by_day.notes: Hire a private driver for the Ubud day trip (IDR 400,000–600,000 for the full day) — much more comfortable than public transport. Wear closed-toe shoes for the rice terrace walk. Dress modestly for temple visits (sarong required — usually provided at entry).

day_by_day.morning: Morning beach yoga session at 7:00 AM — either resort-led or join a local yoga studio class near the beach (IDR 100,000–150,000 drop-in). Focus on a flow or vinyasa practice as the sun rises over the ocean. Follow with a mindful meditation walk along the shoreline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a nearby coastal village by bicycle or scooter (rental IDR 60,000–80,000/day for scooter). Visit local temples, small fishing harbors, and hidden beach coves. Stop at a local coconut grove for fresh young coconut.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks at a rooftop bar or beach club with panoramic ocean views. Watch the golden Bali sunset with a fresh fruit cocktail or Bintang beer.

meals.breakfast: Post-yoga smoothie and avocado toast at a beachside health café — IDR 60,000–90,000
meals.lunch: Local warung lunch during the village exploration — nasi goreng (fried rice) with egg, IDR 25,000–40,000
meals.dinner: Mid-range restaurant dinner — fresh tuna steak with local spices and vegetable sides, IDR 140,000–200,000

day_by_day.notes: If renting a scooter, ensure you have an international driving permit and always wear a helmet. Bali traffic can be unpredictable — ride cautiously. The 30mm monthly rainfall means brief afternoon showers are possible; carry a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Tanah Lot Temple — one of Bali's most iconic sea temples perched on a rocky outcrop (IDR 60,000 entry). Arrive early (8:00–9:00 AM) to beat crowds. The temple is surrounded by crashing waves and offers spectacular coastal scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to a nearby black sand beach or hidden cove for a relaxed afternoon swim and sunbathing. Many of Bali's lesser-known beaches are quieter and equally beautiful. Bring a good book and enjoy the peaceful warm afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Cooking class experience — join a Balinese cooking class (IDR 350,000–500,000) where you'll visit a local market, learn about spices, and cook traditional dishes like sate lilit, lawar, and pandan cake. Eat your creations for dinner!

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — Balinese jajan pasar (traditional sweet snacks) and fresh juice
meals.lunch: Beachside café lunch near the black sand beach — grilled corn, fresh fruit, and iced tea, IDR 50,000–80,000
meals.dinner: Your own Balinese cooking class feast — included in the class price

day_by_day.notes: Tanah Lot is most dramatic at high tide when surrounded by water. Check tide times before visiting. Book the cooking class in advance as popular classes fill up quickly. This is a wonderful mid-trip cultural immersion experience.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day beach relaxation day — your mid-trip rest day. Spend the morning completely unwinding on the resort's beachfront. Read, swim, journal, or simply do nothing. This is intentional downtime to recharge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Indulge in a resort spa afternoon — try a traditional Balinese boreh body scrub (ground rice, ginger, and spices) followed by a floral bath (IDR 200,000–350,000 for a package). This ancient ritual is deeply relaxing and great for the skin.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a beachfront bonfire or live music event at a nearby beach club (many venues host free or low-cost events on weekends). Enjoy local Balinese musicians or a DJ set with the sound of the ocean in the background.

meals.breakfast: Lazy resort breakfast — fresh papaya, yogurt, granola, and Balinese coffee (kopi Bali)
meals.lunch: Pool or beach bar lunch at the resort — club sandwich or fresh spring rolls, IDR 80,000–130,000
meals.dinner: Dinner at a popular mid-range restaurant nearby — wood-fired pizza or pasta for a Western comfort option, IDR 120,000–180,000

day_by_day.notes: Rest days are essential on longer trips. Listen to your body. The warm 25°C weather is perfect for lounging. Stay well hydrated throughout the day — tropical heat can be deceptively draining even in comfortable temperatures.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning Mount Batur sunrise trek — depart from the resort by 1:30–2:00 AM for the 2-hour drive to the trailhead. Begin the 2-hour hike to the summit (1,717m) arriving for a breathtaking sunrise above the clouds over the volcanic caldera. (IDR 400,000–600,000 with guide)
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend the volcano and stop at natural hot springs at the base of Mount Batur for a soothing soak (IDR 75,000–150,000). The mineral-rich geothermal waters are perfect for tired legs. Drive back to the resort and rest.
day_by_day.evening: Early dinner and early bedtime to recover from the pre-dawn adventure. Enjoy a quiet, nourishing meal and gentle stretching before sleep.

meals.breakfast: Sunrise breakfast on the volcano summit — your guide will typically prepare eggs cooked in volcanic steam and toast (usually included in trek fee)
meals.lunch: Post-hot-springs lunch at a local restaurant near Kintamani — babi guling (suckling pig) or vegetarian options, IDR 70,000–110,000
meals.dinner: Light dinner at the resort — vegetable soup, steamed fish, and rice, IDR 90,000–140,000

day_by_day.notes: This is the most physically demanding day of the trip. Book your guide the day before through your resort or a reputable trekking company. Bring warm layers (it's cold at the summit before sunrise), a headlamp, and sturdy shoes. Not recommended if you have mobility issues.

day_by_day.morning: Gentle recovery morning yoga — a slow yin or restorative yoga class to ease sore muscles from the trek (7:30 AM at the resort pavilion or a nearby studio). Focus on hip openers, hamstring stretches, and deep breathing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local Balinese healer (Balian) for a traditional blessing and energy healing session — a deeply authentic cultural experience (IDR 150,000–300,000 donation/fee). Alternatively, visit a beautiful Balinese Hindu temple complex such as Pura Besakih (the Mother Temple) for cultural exploration.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset dinner cruise along the Bali coastline — enjoy a 2-hour boat trip with dinner, live music, and stunning ocean views as the sun sets (IDR 400,000–700,000 per person). A romantic and memorable mid-range splurge.

meals.breakfast: Nourishing post-recovery breakfast — banana pancakes, peanut butter, and fresh juice at a local café, IDR 55,000–80,000
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the temple or healer — vegetable curry and coconut rice, IDR 50,000–75,000
meals.dinner: Included on the sunset dinner cruise — usually a buffet of local and international dishes

day_by_day.notes: Book the sunset dinner cruise at least 2 days in advance. If visiting Pura Besakih, a sarong and sash are mandatory (available to rent at the entrance for a small fee). The healer experience is deeply personal — approach with an open and respectful mindset.

day_by_day.morning: Morning stand-up paddleboarding (SUP) lesson or session on the calm morning ocean (IDR 200,000–300,000 for 1.5 hours with instructor). The ocean is typically glassy and calm in the early morning — perfect for paddleboarding along the coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a nearby waterfall — Bali has stunning hidden waterfalls within an hour or two of coastal areas (e.g., Sekumpul or Gitgit Waterfall, IDR 20,000–50,000 entry). Trek through lush jungle to reach the falls and swim in the natural pools.
day_by_day.evening: Final big cultural night out — enjoy a traditional Legong or Barong dance performance at a local cultural center (IDR 100,000–150,000). Follow with dinner at a well-regarded local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Pre-SUP light breakfast — toast, fruit, and Balinese coffee at the resort
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch near the waterfall — buy fresh snacks from a local stall: spring rolls, fruit, and coconut water, IDR 40,000–70,000
meals.dinner: Dinner at a highly-rated local restaurant — rijsttafel (Indonesian rice table with multiple small dishes), IDR 180,000–280,000

day_by_day.notes: Wear water shoes for the waterfall trek as paths can be slippery. The jungle trek to some waterfalls can be steep — wear appropriate footwear. Check weather conditions before heading out as brief afternoon rain (30mm monthly average) can make trails muddy.

day_by_day.morning: Final beach morning — spend your last full morning on the beach doing whatever you love most. Swim, snorkel, meditate, or simply lie in the warm Bali sun. Take a long walk along the shoreline and collect memories (and maybe some shells).
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at a local art market or boutique shops near the resort. Pick up Balinese crafts, silver jewelry, essential oils, batik fabric, or locally made chocolates and coffee as gifts. Pack thoughtfully.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell sunset ceremony — many resorts offer a private beach setup for a special farewell dinner. Alternatively, choose your favorite restaurant from the trip for a final celebratory dinner. Reflect on your 13-day Bali journey.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast — treat yourself to the complete spread on your last full day
meals.lunch: Lunch at your favorite warung or café from the trip — revisit a spot you loved
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a beachfront restaurant — lobster or fresh catch of the day with Balinese spices, a mid-range splurge at IDR 250,000–400,000

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your departure transfer and flight details today. Pack your bags tonight to avoid morning rush. Leave a review for your favorite local businesses — it supports the Balinese community. Check resort checkout time for tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise yoga on the beach — one last session to honor your body and the beautiful journey. Practice gratitude meditation facing the ocean as the sun rises for the last time on this trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Depending on your departure flight time, enjoy a final coffee and light snack at a beachside café. Take one last walk along the beach before heading to the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Ngurah Rai International Airport. Depart Bali with a heart full of memories, a body recharged by yoga and ocean air, and a deeper connection to one of the world's most magical islands.

meals.breakfast: Final Balinese breakfast — nasi jinggo (small portions of rice with sides wrapped in banana leaf) from a local street vendor, IDR 10,000–15,000 each
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport or a café near the resort before departure — IDR 80,000–150,000
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at the airport at least 3 hours before international departure. Bali airport can be busy — factor in traffic during peak hours. Keep some Indonesian Rupiah for last-minute purchases or tips. Most importantly — start planning your return trip to Bali!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Bali Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled – flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled – in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Ngurah Rai International Airport at 22:30. Meet private airport transfer arranged by Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a smooth, air-conditioned luxury vehicle ride to the resort. Check in, receive a welcome amenity (tropical fruit platter and sparkling wine), and settle into your beachfront suite.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable – in transit
meals.lunch: Not applicable – in transit
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome snack platter and herbal tea provided by the resort upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Request a late check-in arrangement in advance. The resort should have a 24-hour concierge. Keep the first night light – hydrate well and rest to recover from travel fatigue. Lay out your itinerary with the concierge team the next morning.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and ease into Bali time. Enjoy a leisurely gourmet breakfast at the resort's oceanfront restaurant with panoramic beachfront views. Afterward, take a gentle 60-minute sunrise yoga session on the private beach deck led by the resort's in-house yoga instructor – perfect for resetting after the long flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at the resort's private beach. Arrange a personalized snorkeling excursion along the nearby reef with resort-provided premium gear. Follow up with a 90-minute Balinese massage at the resort's luxury spa to release travel tension.
day_by_day.evening: Freshen up and enjoy a sunset cocktail at the resort's infinity pool bar overlooking the Indian Ocean. Dine at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant featuring contemporary Indonesian cuisine with a tasting menu and wine pairing.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet buffet at the resort's oceanfront restaurant – tropical fruits, eggs Benedict, freshly baked pastries, Balinese jamu juice
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch – grilled seafood platter, fresh coconut, and tropical salads at the resort's pool bar
meals.dinner: Signature tasting menu at the resort's fine-dining restaurant – expect dishes like slow-cooked duck betutu, prawn satay, and black rice pudding with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: This is a gentle recovery and orientation day. Avoid overscheduling. Confirm all upcoming activities and reservations with the concierge. Weather expected: warm, around 25°C, ideal beach conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Begin with a 75-minute sunrise Vinyasa yoga class on the resort's beachfront pavilion. After yoga, enjoy breakfast before embarking on a private guided tour to the iconic Tanah Lot Sea Temple – one of Bali's most sacred and photogenic landmarks. Arrive early to beat crowds and enjoy the dramatic coastal scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the nearby Beraban Village for an authentic cultural walk with a private guide. Explore traditional Balinese architecture, local artisan workshops, and rice paddies. Return to the resort for a refreshing dip in the pool.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy pre-dinner drinks at a premium beach club near the resort (such as Finns Beach Club or a similar luxury venue). Dine at a high-end restaurant in Seminyak or Canggu featuring modern Asian fusion cuisine with ocean views.

meals.breakfast: Post-yoga smoothie bowls, avocado toast, and freshly brewed Balinese kopi at the resort
meals.lunch: Traditional Balinese rijsttafel (rice table) at a premium local restaurant near Tanah Lot
meals.dinner: Modern Asian fusion at a top-rated Seminyak restaurant – think wagyu beef rendang, lobster laksa, and artisan desserts

day_by_day.notes: Tanah Lot is best visited in the morning. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the cultural village tour. Private guided transport is recommended – arrange through the concierge. Sun protection essential: SPF 50, hat, and sunglasses.

day_by_day.morning: Morning meditation and breathwork session on the beach at 6:30 AM led by the resort's wellness instructor. Followed by a nutritious breakfast. Then depart on a private half-day excursion to Uluwatu Temple, perched dramatically on a 70-meter clifftop above the Indian Ocean. Explore the temple grounds and enjoy sweeping ocean panoramas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the famous Padang Padang Beach or Dreamland Beach (both premium, less-crowded options in the Bukit Peninsula). Swim, sunbathe, and enjoy the crystal-clear waters. Arrange a private surf lesson with a certified instructor if desired.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the legendary Kecak Fire Dance performance at Uluwatu at sunset – one of Bali's most spectacular cultural experiences. Afterward, dine at a clifftop fine-dining restaurant in Uluwatu with dramatic ocean views.

meals.breakfast: Açaí bowls, poached eggs, Balinese black rice porridge, and fresh tropical juices at the resort
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish and seafood at a beachside premium warung near Padang Padang
meals.dinner: Clifftop dining at a luxury Uluwatu restaurant – grilled lobster, Balinese spiced lamb chops, and artisanal cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Book Kecak Dance tickets in advance – it sells out quickly, especially in peak season. Wear a sarong when entering the temple (available to borrow at the entrance). Monkeys are present at Uluwatu – keep bags and accessories secure.

day_by_day.morning: Full-morning immersive yoga and sound healing retreat session at the resort or a nearby premium yoga studio (such as The Yoga Barn or a private wellness villa). This 3-hour session includes Yin yoga, crystal bowl sound bath, and guided meditation – deeply restorative.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon at leisure – enjoy the resort's luxury amenities including the spa, private beach, and infinity pool. Optionally, book a private paddleboarding or kayaking session along the coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Romantic private beach dinner arranged by the resort – a bespoke table set on the sand with tiki torches, a personalized menu, and a dedicated butler. Perfect for a special evening under the Bali stars.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-yoga breakfast – herbal teas, fresh fruit, and overnight oats at the resort
meals.lunch: Healthy wellness lunch at the resort's health-conscious café – grain bowls, cold-pressed juices, and raw desserts
meals.dinner: Private bespoke beach dinner – curated 5-course menu featuring Balinese and international cuisine with champagne

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the private beach dinner at least 2 days in advance with the resort's concierge. Specify any dietary preferences. This is an ideal evening for couples or anyone seeking a deeply memorable dining experience.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early on a private day trip to Ubud – Bali's cultural heartland (approximately 1.5 hours by private car). Begin with a visit to the Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary, then explore the iconic Ubud Royal Palace (Puri Saren Agung) and the vibrant Ubud Art Market for premium handcrafted souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy a private guided walk through the breathtaking Tegallalang Rice Terraces – UNESCO-recognized and among Bali's most iconic landscapes. Afterward, visit a premium Balinese cooking class or artisan workshop (silver jewelry making or batik painting).
day_by_day.evening: Dine at one of Ubud's world-renowned fine-dining restaurants – such as Locavore (if reservations available) or a comparable premium farm-to-table venue. Return to the resort by private car.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure – continental spread with Balinese coffee
meals.lunch: Farm-to-table lunch at a premium Ubud restaurant overlooking the rice terraces – organic Balinese cuisine
meals.dinner: Fine dining in Ubud at a top-tier restaurant – tasting menu featuring hyper-local Balinese ingredients, rare spices, and paired natural wines

day_by_day.notes: Book Ubud restaurant reservations well in advance – top venues fill up quickly. Wear comfortable shoes for the rice terrace walk. Bring a light layer as Ubud can be slightly cooler than the coast, especially in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Morning yoga flow session on the resort's beach pavilion at sunrise. After breakfast, take a private boat charter to explore the stunning coastline and nearby hidden sea caves and secluded beaches accessible only by water. Snorkel in pristine waters with vibrant marine life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort and indulge in a full luxury spa afternoon – choose from a Balinese deep tissue massage, a traditional lulur body scrub (Javanese royal treatment), and a floral bath ritual. The complete package takes approximately 3 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a premium rooftop sunset social at a nearby luxury hotel or beach club. Enjoy handcrafted cocktails and small plates. Later, dine at a beachfront seafood restaurant with a live acoustic Balinese music performance.

meals.breakfast: Post-yoga breakfast at the resort – smoked salmon eggs Benedict, tropical fruit platter, and Balinese turmeric latte
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood BBQ lunch on the private boat charter – grilled prawns, fish satay, and tropical fruit served onboard
meals.dinner: Premium beachfront seafood restaurant – whole grilled barramundi, tiger prawn curry, and coconut panna cotta

day_by_day.notes: Confirm private boat charter weather conditions the night before. The spa package should be booked 24 hours in advance. Midpoint of the trip – a great time to check in with your overall wellbeing and adjust the remaining itinerary if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise beach walk followed by a 90-minute Ashtanga yoga masterclass with a visiting master instructor (arranged by the resort or a nearby premium wellness studio). Post-yoga, enjoy a nourishing breakfast and then depart on a private guided tour to Besakih Temple – Bali's largest and holiest Hindu temple complex on the slopes of Mount Agung.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the East Bali coastline, stopping at the serene and less-touristed Candidasa area. Visit the scenic Tirta Gangga Water Palace – a stunning royal garden with tiered fountains and ornamental pools. Enjoy a leisurely stroll through the grounds.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Enjoy a private in-suite dinner or dine at the resort's premium restaurant with a specially curated East Balinese-inspired menu. Wind down with a nightcap at the resort's bar.

meals.breakfast: Nourishing post-yoga breakfast – green smoothie bowl, poached eggs on sourdough, and fresh juices
meals.lunch: Traditional Balinese lunch at a premium restaurant near Tirta Gangga – bebek betutu (slow-cooked duck), sate lilit, and black rice pudding
meals.dinner: In-suite or resort restaurant private dinner – personalized 4-course menu with Balinese and Mediterranean influences

day_by_day.notes: Besakih Temple requires a sarong and respectful attire. Hire a certified local guide at the temple to navigate the complex and gain cultural insight. East Bali roads can be winding – allow extra travel time.

day_by_day.morning: Begin with a morning meditation and journaling session on your private beachfront terrace. After breakfast, enjoy a premium surf lesson at a nearby world-class surf break with a private certified instructor. Suitable for all levels – beginners will be taken to gentle breaks, while experienced surfers can access reef breaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: After surfing, freshen up and explore the local beach town near the resort – browse boutique shops, local galleries, and artisan stores. Enjoy a leisurely afternoon at a nearby luxury beach club with a private cabana, pool, and cocktail service.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset yoga and breathwork session on the beach. Dine at a premium restaurant in Seminyak or Petitenget area – known for Bali's most sophisticated dining scene.

meals.breakfast: Pre-surf energizing breakfast – banana pancakes, protein smoothie, and Balinese kopi
meals.lunch: Poolside lunch at the luxury beach club – fresh ceviche, truffle fries, and tropical cocktails
meals.dinner: Upscale Seminyak dining – duck confit with Balinese spices, grilled octopus, and premium dessert selection with wine

day_by_day.notes: Confirm surf lesson suitability with the instructor based on experience level. Book beach club cabana in advance during peak season. Seminyak restaurants are popular – reservations recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Full-morning premium wellness experience: begin with a 60-minute Kundalini yoga session, followed by a guided Balinese healing ceremony with a local Balian (traditional healer) – a deeply spiritual and authentic cultural experience. This is a rare, meaningful insight into Balinese Hindu spiritual practices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the picturesque Jatiluwih Rice Terraces – a UNESCO World Heritage Site offering expansive, panoramic views of traditional subak irrigation systems. Enjoy a leisurely guided walk through the terraces with a knowledgeable local guide.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a private couples' or solo sunset spa ritual – flower bath, aromatherapy massage, and champagne. Dine at the resort's beachfront restaurant under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Light and grounding pre-ceremony breakfast – herbal porridge, fresh papaya, and ceremonial cacao
meals.lunch: Organic farm lunch at a premium warung near Jatiluwih – local vegetables, tofu, tempeh, and hand-pounded sambal
meals.dinner: Resort's beachfront restaurant – grilled seafood, Balinese spiced lamb, and tropical sorbet under the stars

day_by_day.notes: The Balian healing ceremony should be arranged through a trusted cultural concierge or the resort – ensure it is conducted respectfully and authentically. Dress modestly for the ceremony. Jatiluwih entrance fee applies.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga on the beach followed by a hearty breakfast. Depart on a private boat excursion to Nusa Penida – one of Bali's most spectacular island destinations. Visit the iconic Kelingking Beach (T-Rex cliff viewpoint), Crystal Bay, and Angel's Billabong natural infinity pool.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nusa Penida with a stop at Broken Beach (Pasih Uug) – a dramatic natural arch formation with turquoise waters. Enjoy a snorkeling session in Crystal Bay where manta rays are occasionally spotted. Return by private speedboat to the mainland.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back at the resort in the late afternoon. Enjoy a relaxing sunset dip in the infinity pool. Dine at a premium Jimbaran Bay seafood restaurant – famous for its beachside grilled seafood experience.

meals.breakfast: Energizing breakfast at the resort – full Balinese breakfast spread with nasi goreng, tropical fruits, and fresh juices
meals.lunch: Packed premium picnic lunch on Nusa Penida – gourmet sandwiches, fresh fruit, and sparkling water arranged by the resort
meals.dinner: Jimbaran Bay beachfront seafood feast – whole grilled lobster, tiger prawns, fish, and clams with traditional sambal and rice

day_by_day.notes: Nusa Penida day trip requires a full day – depart by 7:30 AM. Wear sturdy footwear as some viewpoints involve steep paths. Book private speedboat in advance. Bring seasickness medication if sensitive to boat travel. Sunscreen and hydration are essential.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day – begin with a slow, reflective morning. Enjoy a 90-minute restorative yoga and Yoga Nidra (yogic sleep) session on the beach pavilion. After breakfast, indulge in a full luxury spa day at the resort – book the resort's signature full-day wellness package including body wrap, facial, scalp treatment, and massage.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the spa, spend the afternoon at your leisure on the private beach. Enjoy the resort's premium amenities one last time – paddleboarding, reading in a beach cabana, or simply soaking in the Bali sunshine. Optional: visit a nearby boutique for last-minute premium Balinese gifts and souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the resort's finest dining venue – request a special table on the beachfront terrace. Opt for the chef's special farewell tasting menu with champagne. After dinner, enjoy a final nightcap at the infinity pool bar under the Bali stars.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent final morning breakfast – eggs royale, fresh pastries, tropical fruit, Balinese coffee, and fresh juices
meals.lunch: Light spa lunch at the resort's wellness café – superfood salads, cold-pressed juices, and raw treats
meals.dinner: Farewell chef's tasting menu at the resort's beachfront fine-dining terrace – 6 courses with champagne and wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time and airport transfer arrangements with the concierge today. Pack non-essential items tonight to ease departure tomorrow. Reflect on the journey and capture final memories of the resort and Bali's magical atmosphere.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise yoga or gentle beach walk at dawn – a peaceful farewell to Bali. Enjoy a last breakfast at the resort. Complete checkout formalities with the concierge team. The resort's private luxury transfer will escort you to Ngurah Rai International Airport in comfort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure – time at the airport. Access the premium airline lounge for refreshments and relaxation before boarding.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Bali, carrying extraordinary memories of beaches, yoga, culture, and luxury from this unforgettable 13-day journey.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at the resort – a personal selection of your favorite dishes from the week
meals.lunch: Premium airport lounge dining or in-flight meal
meals.dinner: In-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before departure for airport check-in and security. The resort's concierge can assist with luggage handling, last-minute purchases, and ensuring a seamless departure. Request a late checkout if your flight allows.
